newsitem.title: USA: Manufactured Home files suit vs Chateau, ROC.
newsitem.headline: Manufactured Home files suit vs Chateau, ROC.

text.p: Manufactured Home Communities Inc said on Wednesday it filed a suit against Chateau Properties Inc and ROC Communities Inc and several Chateau board members over their agreed merger.
Mobile home park operator Chateau said last week its board of directors unanimously approved a revised merger agreement with ROC, rejecting a proposal from Manufactured and Sun Communities Inc.

"We are forced to take this action in response to the drastic steps taken last week by Chateau and ROC," Chairman Samuel Zell said in a statement. "Their restructured merger disenfranchises Chateau's shareholders and ultimately reallocates tax liability from Chateau insiders to the shareholders."
Manufactured said it had filed a suit against Chateau board members John Boll, C.G. Kellogg, Jay Rudolph, Gebran Anton Jr., James Lane, Kenneth Myers and Edward Allen in a Maryland district court.
"From the outset we expected that Chateau's Board would recognize the superiority of Manufactured Home all-cash offer," Zell said. "Apparently the Chateau Board has other priorities."

Manufactured Homes, which launched a $26 per share offer for Chateau on September 4, said its lawsuit sought a temporary restraining order to stop Chateau and its board members from spending company assets or otherwise carrying out the purchase of 1.45 million outstanding Chateau common stock.
The order also sought to prevent ROC from buying 350,000 outstanding Chateau shares.

Manufactured also said it was seeking various other forms of judicial relief in connection with an alleged plan by Chateau insiders, aided by ROC, to block Manufactured's tender offer by misrepresenting material facts.
Chateau was not immediately available to comment.

Chateau said last week it intended to defend itself against a class action suit filed on September 12 alleging its directors violated their fiduciary duties by not endorsing the Manufactured Home offer. Chateau also said it filed a suit against Manufactured on September 17, alleging its $26 per share tender offer was made in violation of U.S. securities law.
